picks.headline: Release of open AI model trained on 17 years of lunar data maps ice, craters and volcanoes
picks.excerpt: NASA and IBM released an open-source lunar foundation model trained on nearly two decades of Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data. It lets researchers identify ice deposits, impact craters and volcanic features with only minimal labeled training data.
picks.rationale: An openly downloadable NASA/IBM foundation model that any lab can fine-tune on a handful of labels — the most immediately usable release in the pool.

picks.headline: An AI tool aims to catch harder-to-detect heart attacks in EKGs
picks.excerpt: The FDA granted a rare de novo clearance to Powerful Medical's 'Queen of Hearts' algorithm, which reads electrocardiograms to flag and triage heart attacks that standard criteria miss. It is one of the first AI tools authorized for occlusion-type infarcts invisible to conventional EKG rules.
picks.rationale: A rare de novo FDA clearance moves AI diagnosis past the pilot stage into authorized clinical use for a failure mode standard EKG rules cannot see.

picks.headline: New AI model for DNA learns from evolution to unlock secrets of the human genome
picks.excerpt: UC Berkeley's GPN-Star, a genomic language model trained on evolutionary signal, outperforms larger rivals at pinpointing the genetic variants behind inherited traits and disease. It does so while requiring far less compute to train than competing genomic foundation models.
picks.rationale: Evolutionary signal beats sheer scale here — a smaller, cheaper genomic model outperforming larger rivals changes what an academic lab can afford to train.

picks.headline: AI extracts interpretable constitutive laws directly from solid-mechanics data
picks.excerpt: A graph-based framework from the Eastern Institute of Technology reads raw material-test data and writes out explicit, physically interpretable equations for how alloy steels, lithium metal and filled rubbers deform. It beat mainstream empirical models on predictive accuracy without becoming a black box.
picks.rationale: It returns readable equations rather than a black box, so engineers can drop the output straight into existing simulation stacks and still audit it.

picks.headline: Lancaster University Leads Project on Quantum Neural Computing
picks.excerpt: Lancaster University is leading IgnisQNC, a EUR 1.88M three-year European project fusing quantum computing with explainable AI. The goal is to turn quantum uncertainty into a computational resource for trustworthy machine learning rather than a source of noise.
picks.rationale: Treating quantum noise as a resource for explainable AI is an inversion of the usual framing, and the only quantum item in a pool otherwise dominated by bio and materials.
